target_customer: Offices and showrooms that pay a flat monthly fee for a tea amenity (earlier plan: cafes hosting kiosks)
problem: Custom loose leaf tea was slow and inconsistent to serve; teaBOT brews a custom blend in under 30 seconds through an app or touchscreen.
business_model: Hardware as a service with monthly fee for offices; earlier revenue share with cafes hosting kiosks
product_category: Food service robot, tea brewing kiosk

founders.name: Rehman Merali
education: University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies, PhD student (robotics, in Prof. Tim Barfoot's lab) at the time of the 2015 article
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as having a PhD in Robotics.

founders.name: Brian Lee
founders.background_notes: High school friend of Merali per the University of Toronto magazine; his mother owns a tea shop in Sudbury, Ontario, which inspired the idea. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Teforia
competitors.what: Home machine that brews loose leaf tea using automated infusion
competitors.traction_then: Pre-order campaign around $300K per a roundup, unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom robotic dispenser with blending and brewing, app and kiosk software; hardware risk but a PhD robotics founder.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware design is copyable by funded rivals; main edge was early placements and branding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Teforia raised more money but is listed as dead by CB Insights; teaBOT survived as a small office amenity business.

market_need_then: Specialty tea was growing in cafes and offices; the founders saw that cafes struggle to offer custom blends and long lines, per University of Toronto magazine.

branding.domain_note: Uses teabot.com (stylised teaBOT); the legal entity is TBOT Inc.

identity.visual_style: Product centered; robot kiosk with app

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch (taste test, 2015), the YC blog, University of Toronto outlets and the Chicago Business Journal (2022).

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that explains the product and drew press; limited evidence of community beyond coverage.

pivots.from: Cafe kiosks that brew custom cups for consumers
pivots.to: Tea robot as an office amenity with flat monthly fee
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; inferred from the 2017 model versus the current website. Date approximate.

outcome_analysis: teaBOT joined YC in Summer 2015 with a custom tea robot for cafes, drew strong early press, then moved to selling an office amenity on a monthly fee. It remains active with logos of large corporate customers but no substantial funding or growth story was found, so the evidence points to a small niche hardware business rather than a venture scale outcome.
notes: Unverified funding: CB Insights shows $120K seed in July 2015, Caplight $265K (investors Zillionize, MaRS JOLT, YC), Bouncewatch and Village about $400K including grants; none confirmed by a press release so none recorded as rounds. A $25K UTIAS Start grant was seen only in a search snippet. The pivot date is approximate and inferred. The Teforia source is dated October 2015, a few months after the batch. The teaBOT site cites a 2015 TechCrunch taste test.
